content: PanoRef multi-origin coverage optimizer review and follow-up. The implementation adds 17 coverage-engine files, a worker, UI, and tests, with joint mode genuinely evaluating candidate pairs rather than greedily selecting the best first origin. Algorithm architecture for normal graybox sets is rated 8/10, correctness of the two search modes 7.5/10, readiness for complex imported sets 4/10, overall promising but not production-ready. Strengths include deterministic surface sampling proportional to world-space area via barycentric coordinates, origin evaluation covering actual segment occlusion, geometric face normals, viewing angle, approximate projected texel density, separate visibility and usable-coverage bitsets, and continuous quality values. The joint-pair mode checks every legal coarse pair, ranks by bitset union, then applies quality and contribution tie-breakers. The shared coarse-to-fine engine uses 4,096 coarse samples, 256 candidates, retained pair seeds, 24,576 fine samples, local offsets, and separate fixed-first and joint branches. Tests cover deterministic sampling, double-sided occlusion, marginal second-origin ranking, non-greedy pair ranking, candidate generation, and both search modes. Blockers: (1) imported sets can produce zero legal candidates because every non-floor scene object's entire AABB is stored as an obstacle, so points inside the AABB get zero clearance and are rejected—this affects complete Maya sets imported as one GLB, room shell and furniture combined into one mesh, concave geometry, L-shaped walls, and any large model whose AABB contains empty navigable space; fix is to use actual geometry clearance (camera sphere/capsule does not intersect nearby triangles) via the coverage BVH through point-to-triangle distance, sphere intersection, or shapecast, with obstacle bounds per connected mesh or spatial cluster, plus a regression test with one imported object containing a room floor, walls, and empty interior. (2) Geometry representation will not scale to heavy imports: every triangle is expanded to a JavaScript object with three independent Vec3 arrays, a normal array, IDs, and area; for 3 million triangles, minimum packed geometry data is ~144 MB (positions 108 MB, normals 36 MB), but the actual representation uses JS objects, arrays, and 64-bit numbers, several times larger, then structured-cloned into the worker with postMessage creating another enormous representation, and the BVH recursively sorts and slices JS index arrays, with every triangle intersection allocating several temporary three-element arrays causing extreme GC pressure; fix is to use compact typed arrays (positions: Float32Array, indices: Uint32Array, normals?: Float32Array, meshRanges: Uint32Array, transforms: Float32Array), transfer ArrayBuffers into the worker rather than cloning nested objects, and for the BVH use three-mesh-bvh, implement a flat typed-array BVH with in-place partitioning, or build per-mesh BVHs from existing indexed geometries, and avoid expanding indexed vertices into three world-space vertex arrays per triangle. (3) Geometry extraction still blocks the main thread because the panel synchronously calls extractCoverageScene(project) before creating/posting to the worker, so the worker keeps the expensive optimizer off the UI thread but not scene recreation, triangle flattening, world-transform application, geometry disposal, or structured cloning; on a complex model the app may freeze before the worker reports its first progress event; fix is to move extraction into the worker or at least make it chunked and yield between meshes. (4) 'Apply to selected panorama pair' is conceptually wrong: the UI allows optimized origins to be written directly into the two existing panorama references via updatePanoReference(primaryPanoId, { origin: originA }) and updatePanoReference(secondaryPanoId, { origin: originB }), but an existing panorama was rendered or generated from its original origin, so changing its metadata does not transform the image into a panorama captured from the new position, merely projecting old pixels from the wrong point and ruining alignment; correct workflow for fixed-first is to preserve the existing panorama and its origin, move the next capture origin to B, render a new graybox panorama, inpaint/generate the new styled panorama, and import it as the secondary panorama; for joint mode, create a two-origin capture plan, move capture origin to A, capture/render A, move to B, capture/render B, and associate each imported result with its actual origin; do not rewrite the origins of already captured panoramas. (5) The reachable upper bound is mathematically inconsistent: reachableCoverage is calculated using the coarse sample bank and all coarse candidates, while the final combined coverage is calculated using a different fine sample bank generated with seed + 1, so the UI can theoretically show Combined coverage: 83%, Reachable upper bound: 80%, Reachable captured: 100%; the clamp hides the impossible ratio but does not repair the incompatible estimates; there is another fixed-first issue where the reachable set is calculated before the arbitrary first origin is evaluated, so the fixed first origin is not included in the reachable upper bound at all; fix is to use a common validation sample bank for both final pair coverage, reachable candidate union, and efficiency, and for fixed-first include the fixed origin in the reachable union, while still using separate coarse and fine search banks internally but reporting metrics on one shared final bank. (6) Fixed-first does not enforce minimum separation: joint mode rejects pairs below minimumOriginSeparation, but fixed-first mode does not; rankSecondOrigins only filters by object identity, not position or distance, so since the first evaluation is a separate object, even an identical candidate position survives; add distance(first.position, candidate.position) >= minimumOriginSeparation, otherwise an open set with little marginal difference could return a nearly duplicate second origin. Important refinements: the 'four-level refinement' is not truly iterative—for every seed, all offsets are generated around the original seed (seed ± spacing/2, seed ± spacing/4, seed ± spacing/8, seed ± spacing/16), but the system does not select the best half-step result and then center the quarter-step search around that new result, so it is still a useful multiresolution neighborhood sample but not the coordinate/pattern refinement described in the plan; a true refinement loop would update the center after every level. Local candidates can float between floors: candidate validation only checks whether a floor exists somewhere below the candidate, and local offsets retain the original Y coordinate, so on sloped terrain or multilevel sets, an offset can move over a lower floor while preserving the upper floor's camera height, leaving the panorama origin floating several meters above the new floor; for each offset, find the floor under the new X/Z, set Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters, then perform clearance. The optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules: the optimizer evaluates angle and texel density, but when both panoramas are visible, the actual shader still blends them only by distance, so the optimizer may prefer a source for its frontal angle while the runtime renderer favors the closer but more grazing source, and the optimized coverage result and the visible result do not fully agree; the shader should use the same approximate quality function and preferably winner-takes-most selection rather than broad continuous averaging. Testing assessment: current tests are good unit tests, but the most dangerous cases are absent: one large imported object containing an entire room, a 100k+ triangle performance fixture, reachableCoverage >= combinedCoverage invariant, fixed-first candidate separation, sloped and multilevel floors, existing panorama origins remaining immutable, and candidate generation inside concave imported geometry; there are no GitHub Actions workflow runs attached to the latest head, so the reported test suite has not been independently enforced in CI. Bottom line: this push is much better than what was reviewed before; the two algorithms are truly implemented, and the joint search is not fake or merely greedy; preserve most of the high-level design; required changes are: replace AABB clearance with actual geometry clearance, replace object-heavy triangle/BVH data with typed arrays and transferable buffers, move extraction into the worker, remove the ability to relocate existing panorama references, recalculate reported metrics on one common sample bank, enforce separation in fixed-first mode, and reproject local refinement candidates onto their floor; after those, the optimizer would be considered a strong, credible feature, but right now it should work nicely on ordinary PanoRef primitive sets, while the exact scenario motivating this feature—a complex imported production set—is where the current implementation is most likely to fail. Follow-up directive: rebase onto main and resolve the PR conflict, add an allowed-floor-region mechanism or at least robust imported-floor component filtering, run one real complex imported-set benchmark and add a full 100K+ optimizer integration test (not merely a BVH-construction test), set a goal to accomplish the above, and when work is complete, spawn a subagent whose job is to disprove that the goal is actually fully complete, have it report back what still is lacking, then fix that, and repeat that process until the subagent is unable to find any holes in the implementation. Implementation actions: removed the stale test guarding the old distance-only blend heuristic, removed the dead shader constant PROJECTED_FALLOFF = 6.0, and replaced the assertion with one that protects the new optimizer-aligned angle/texel-quality selection and dominance modes (projectedQualityAt, projectedBlendMode == 2 ? 1.15 : 1.0, projectedBlendMode == 3 ? 1.15 : 1.0, and not.toContain('projectedConfidence')); the targeted regression test (tests/multiOriginInteraction.test.ts, 36 tests) passed. Full CI run: unit tests (42 test files, 371 tests) all passed, including projectionCoverage.test.ts (10 tests, 39235ms) which runs both complete optimizer modes on a 100k+ triangle indexed fixture, occlusionPixel.test.ts (1 test, 3973ms) real WebGL pixel readback, projectedStyleCompile.test.ts (2 tests, 3934ms) real WebGL compile gate, and projectedReceive.test.ts (1 test, 4309ms) real WebGL pixel readback; lint (tsc --noEmit) passed; build (vite build) passed.
